Calendar and Islamic occasions

On this page
  • The calendar screen
  • Dates & age
  • The Hijri calendar
  • Calendar settings
  • Islamic occasions

The Calendar tile opens one screen with several modes: prayer times, dates and age, the Sun, day and night, the Moon, eclipses, the sky and geographic information. Every mode keeps the month calendar at the bottom, and every mode follows the day you select there.

This chapter covers the calendar itself, the Dates & age mode, the Hijri calendar choices and the Islamic occasions. The prayer mode is in Prayer times; the astronomy modes are in Sky, Moon and astronomy.

The calendar screen

  • The title bar shows the mode's icon and name, in the mode's own colour. Tap the name to list all the modes and choose one, or use the double arrows on either side to step to the previous or next mode.
  • The sub-views under the title bar switch between the mode's pages, for example Times and Chart.
  • The month calendar at the bottom: tap a day to select it. Today is outlined, the selected day is filled, and the days of the next and previous months are faded. Fridays are shown in the accent colour.

The modes and their sub-views:

ModeSub-views
Dates & ageDates, Converter, Age, Chart
Prayer timesTimes, Chart
SunDay, Chart, Seasons
Day & nightTimes, Dial, Year, Map
MoonPosition, Phases, Distance, Crescent
EclipsesList, Map
SkyPlanets
Geographic infoMagnetism

The calendar opens on the last mode you used. To open it always on the same mode, set Settings → Calendar → Open Calendar on.

The month calendar

  • The arrows beside the month title move one month back or forward.
  • Each day shows the date of the main calendar in large type and the date of the second calendar in small type. Choose them in Settings → Calendar → Main calendar and Second calendar.
  • The weekday the rows start on is set in Week starts on (Sunday by default).

Choose a date

Tap the month title (or the large date at the top of the Dates and Age pages) to open Choose a date:

  1. Choose the calendar at the top: Gregorian, Hijri or Solar Hijri. The line under it shows the full date as you turn the wheels.
  2. Turn the day, month and year wheels by swiping or scrolling. To type a number instead, tap the value in the middle of a wheel.
  3. Tap OK. Cancel leaves everything as it was.

If the wheels point at a day that does not exist in that calendar, the sheet says "Not a valid date in this calendar."

Dates & age

Dates

The selected day's weekday as a headline, then its date in the Gregorian, Hijri and Solar Hijri calendars, the Julian Day Number, the Day of the year and the ISO week. Tap the headline to choose another day.

Converter

To convert a date from one calendar to the others:

  1. Choose the calendar of the date you have: Gregorian, Hijri (your chosen Hijri calendar), Solar Hijri or Julian.
  2. Type the Day, Month and Year.
  3. Read the same day in all four calendars.
  4. Tap Show in calendar to select that day in the month calendar.

Age

The selected day is treated as a birth date. To find an age:

  1. Tap the headline date and choose the birth date (in any of the three calendars).
  2. Read the birth date in each calendar, then the Gregorian age, Hijri age and Solar Hijri age in years, months and days, the Total days, and the Next birthday (Gregorian) and Next birthday (Hijri).

The age is counted on today. To count it on another day, tap Change beside Age on and choose the day; Today brings it back.

Chart

A picture of the selected day's whole year at your place: the months across, the hours of the day up, and the night, twilight and daylight of every day as coloured bands. A line marks the selected day and another the time now; the Local time and UTC clocks are shown under it. Tap the chart to select the day under your finger.

The Hijri calendar

Taqwim offers three ways to count the Hijri calendar. Choose one in Settings → Calendar → Hijri calendar:

ChoiceHow it works
Umm al-Qura (default)Saudi Arabia's official calendar, from its published table. It covers the years 1300 to 1600 AH; outside them no Hijri date is shown.
Tabular (civil)A fixed arithmetic rule: months of 30 and 29 days in turn, with 11 leap years in every 30 years, counted from Friday 16 July 622.
Tabular (astronomical)The same rule counted from one day earlier, Thursday 15 July 622, so its dates usually run one day ahead of the civil one.

None of these follows the actual sighting of the new crescent where you live. In many countries the month begins when the crescent is seen, so the local date can differ by a day from any computed calendar.

To match your local calendar:

  1. Open Settings → Calendar.
  2. Under Hijri adjustment, tap − or + to move every Hijri date by up to three days either way.

The adjustment applies everywhere in the app: the dates panel, the month calendar, the converter and the Islamic occasions.

To see when the new crescent can be seen at your place, use the Moon mode's Crescent page. See Sky, Moon and astronomy.

Islamic occasions

The Islamic occasions tile on the home screen lists the occasions of one Hijri year:

  • Islamic New Year
  • Ashura
  • First of Ramadan
  • Eid al-Fitr
  • First day of Hajj
  • Day of Arafah
  • Eid al-Adha

At the top, Next occasion shows the coming one in large type, with how long remains ("In 5 days", "Tomorrow", "Today"), its Hijri date with the weekday, and its Gregorian date. Below it, the whole year is listed; past occasions are dimmed, and today's is marked.

  • The screen opens on the year whose next occasion is still ahead. Use the arrows beside the title to see the previous or next year.
  • The dates follow your Hijri calendar and Hijri adjustment, as the line under the list reminds you: "The actual date follows the sighting of the crescent."
  • With Umm al-Qura, years outside 1300–1600 AH show "This year is outside the chosen Hijri calendar's range."
